question.problem: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $-3\le 2x-7\le 1$ or $2+3x<2.$
question.worked_solution:
We start by solving $-3\le 2x-7\le 1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-3 & \le 2x-7\le 1 \\ 4 & \le 2x\le 8 \\ 2 & \le x\le 4\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252742/assets/909a1923438f6bf6931373c1a29cde24cd6ed08166c96769afa10a9a28696113.png)

Then, we solve $2+3x<2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2+3x & <2 \\ 3x & <0 \\ \frac{3x}{3} & <\frac{0}{3} \\ x & <0\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252742/assets/daafda364f7c22d6db174e8fcc63092b754ca124854aa24a18bb7f0df024981c.png)

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252742/assets/b84ab4b3eeab7754193a0a41a2a1dc86338f7f0bed682b86b74fbe83cab6324d.png)

Therefore, the final solution is $x<0$ or $2\le x\le 4.$ We can write this using interval notation as $(-\infty ,0)\cup [2,4].$
